payload.name: Include State and Interest Memories for Favorite Questions
payload.description: When a favorite/preferred question returns no relevant evidence after searching preference/profile memories, also search state/interest memories using enjoyment-related terms.
content: If a question asks about a person's favorite or preferred item and a preference/profile search returns no memory naming the requested category, run an additional hybrid search including memory_kind 'state' with terms like 'enjoys', 'interested in', 'into', 'likes', or 'loves' combined with the person's name and the item category.

Treat a state/interest memory explicitly naming the specific item(s) the person is into or enjoys as authoritative evidence for the favorite answer when it directly names the requested category; do not use generic interest statements that lack specific items.
Stop once the retrieved state/interest memories cover all specific items asked about, or after one or two supplementary searches; do not expand exhaustively.

solves: When a question asks about a person's favorite or preferred item, the evidence may be stored in a state/interest memory rather than an explicit preference memory. Searches restricted to preference and profile kinds can miss this evidence, causing an incorrect 'no evidence' answer. This skill broadens retrieval to include state/interest memories with enjoyment-related language.
